title: Sylvester (31 December)
hookLine: the pope of Constantine's time, kept on New Year's Eve

lines: A PARTY NAMED FOR A POPE?
cards: Why would a New Year's party be named after a pope? In Vienna or Berlin, ask what the night of 31 December is called and you may hear a name instead of a date: Silvester. In Warsaw, Sylwester.
Fireworks, countdowns, glasses raised at midnight, and the whole night carries a saint's name. He was a pope, and his feast falls on the last day of the calendar year.

teach.b: Sylvester was bishop of Rome in the time of the emperor Constantine, when persecution gave way to imperial favor.
Christians who once could lose their property or their lives for gathering to worship now watched an emperor build churches. For a pope, everything was changing.
The honest part: we know surprisingly little for certain about Sylvester himself. The old book of the popes, the Liber Pontificalis, lists churches built and gifts given in his time.
When the bishops gathered at Nicaea to answer who Christ is, the usual account is that Sylvester didn't go himself but sent representatives. Where the facts ran thin, stories grew.
A later legend says he cured Constantine of a disease and baptized him in Rome. The older histories tell it differently: the emperor was baptized near the end of his life, far from Rome.

So the Church remembers a pope partly hidden behind his own legends. Maybe that fits a man kept on New Year's Eve. From its last night, a year can look the same way: a few moments stay clear, and the rest blurs.
A psalm in the Douay-Rheims says to God, "Thou shalt bless the crown of the year of thy goodness." The crown of the year: the whole circle of it, clear days and blurry ones, held up and blessed.
Sylvester's feast puts a saint at the very edge of the calendar, and some Catholics read that as a sign that even the year's last night belongs to God.

how: Catholics may keep Saint Sylvester's memorial on 31 December; in some parishes the year ends with Mass or with a hymn of thanksgiving, the Te Deum, sung on the evening of the last day of the year.

games.q: you're Sylvester, bishop of Rome. bishops are gathering at Nicaea to settle who Christ is. what do you do?
o: make the long journey and preside
games.why: the usual account is that he sent representatives. the pope himself stayed in Rome.

practice: Let this year go by like pages turning, without stopping to fix anything: a morning you remember, a person who showed up, something that went wrong and turned out survivable.
When a memory comes back, stay with it for a breath and say thank you, inside.
If you pray, offer the whole year back to God, the clear parts and the blurry ones; if you don't, simply let the thank-yous pile up, one memory at a time.

wordCard.voice: Sylvester. The pope of Constantine's time, little known for certain and wrapped in legend, whose feast closes the calendar year. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: the saint's name; in some countries it is also the name of New Year's Eve.

carryVoice: Your line: the year's last saint. Even the calendar's final night has a name. That's today, done.
